citation: Huang NE, Shen Z, Long SR, Wu MC, Shih HH, Zheng Q, Yen NC, Tung CC, Liu HH. The empirical mode decomposition and the Hilbert spectrum for nonlinear and non-stationary time series analysis. Proc R Soc Lond A Math Phys Eng Sci. 1998;454(1971):903-995.
design: Foundational methodological and theoretical study with synthetic nonlinear oscillators and physical time series
signal_type: Synthetic nonlinear/non-stationary time series (Stokes wave, Duffing oscillator, Lorenz system) and physical signals
decomposition: Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) + Hilbert Transform (HHT)
parameters_reported: Single-sift plain EMD; cubic spline upper/lower envelope interpolation; Cauchy-type SD stopping rule between 0.2 and 0.3
key_finding: Introduced adaptive sifting of nonlinear, non-stationary signals into Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs) admitting physically meaningful instantaneous frequency via the Hilbert transform.

citation: Deering R, Kaiser JF. The use of a masking signal to improve empirical mode decomposition. In: Proceedings of the IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing (ICASSP); 2005 Mar 18-23; Philadelphia, PA, USA. IEEE; 2005. Vol. 4, p. iv/485-iv/488.
design: Methodological algorithm development and synthetic benchmark study
signal_type: Synthetic multi-component and intermittent time series with closely spaced frequencies
decomposition: Masking Empirical Mode Decomposition (Masking EMD)
parameters_reported: 2 complementary sifts per mode (+m(t) and -m(t) deterministic sinusoidal masking signal with frequency slightly above highest component frequency)
key_finding: Adding and subtracting a deterministic sinusoidal masking signal before sifting prevents lower-frequency components from leaking into higher-frequency IMFs and resolves mode mixing without stochastic residuals.

citation: Wu Z, Huang NE. Ensemble empirical mode decomposition: a noise-assisted data analysis method. Adv Adapt Data Anal. 2009;1(1):1-41.
design: Foundational methodological and noise-assisted algorithmic study
signal_type: Synthetic intermittent signals, white noise, climatic records, and human speech time series
decomposition: Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD)
parameters_reported: Ensemble size N = 100 to 500 trials; added white noise amplitude epsilon = 0.2 of signal SD; S-number stopping rule (S = 4 to 8)
key_finding: Adding independent white noise realizations populates the entire time-frequency space uniformly, leveraging dyadic filter-bank properties of EMD to eliminate mode mixing.

citation: Huang NE, Wu Z, Long SR, Arnold KC, Chen X, Blank K. On instantaneous frequency. Adv Adapt Data Anal. 2009;1(2):177-229.
design: Mathematical and methodological theory study
signal_type: Synthetic AM-FM signals and nonlinear oscillators
decomposition: EMD + Normalised Hilbert Transform (NHT) and Direct Quadrature (DQ)
parameters_reported: Iterative empirical envelope normalisation using cubic spline interpolation of local maxima of |IMF(t)| until maxima equal unity
key_finding: Demonstrated that applying the Hilbert transform directly violates the Bedrosian theorem when AM and FM overlap; empirical envelope normalisation rigorously separates AM envelope from unit-modulus carrier.

citation: Zhang Q, Shi Y, Teng D, Dinh A, Ko SB, Chen L, Basran J, Dal Bello-Haas V, Choi Y. Pulse transit time-based blood pressure estimation using Hilbert-Huang transform. Annu Int Conf IEEE Eng Med Biol Soc. 2009;2009:1785-1788.
design: Biomedical signal processing methodology study
signal_type: Human electrocardiogram (ECG) and photoplethysmography (PPG) signals
decomposition: Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) + Hilbert-Huang Transform (HHT)
parameters_reported: Not reported
key_finding: Demonstrated that HHT adaptive decomposition isolates intrinsic cardiac pulse components from motion artifacts and baseline wander in non-stationary ECG and PPG recordings.

citation: Yeh JR, Shieh JS, Huang NE. Complementary ensemble empirical mode decomposition: a novel noise enhanced data analysis method. Adv Adapt Data Anal. 2010;2(2):135-156.
design: Methodological algorithm development study
signal_type: Synthetic nonlinear/non-stationary time series and physiological recordings
decomposition: Complementary Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (CEEMD)
parameters_reported: Complementary positive and negative white-noise pairs (+w_i(t), -w_i(t)); ensemble size N pairs; noise amplitude ~0.1-0.2 SD
key_finding: Adding white noise in complementary pairs cancels residual white noise in the reconstructed signal exactly while retaining mode-mixing suppression with fewer trials.

citation: Torres ME, Colominas MA, Schlotthauer G, Flandrin P. A complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise. In: Proceedings of the 2011 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP); 2011 May 22-27; Prague, Czech Republic. IEEE; 2011. p. 4144-4147.
design: Foundational methodological algorithm study
signal_type: Synthetic impulse/sinusoid mixture and human ECG signal
decomposition: Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN)
parameters_reported: Ensemble size I = 50 to 500 realizations; stage-wise adaptive noise amplitude epsilon_k (~0.2 of stage residue SD)
key_finding: Decomposing stage-specific EMD modes of white noise added to sequential residues guarantees exact reconstruction and resolves mode mixing with fewer ensemble trials.

citation: Mariyappa N, Sengottuvel S, Parasakthi C, Gireesan K, Janawadkar MP, Radhakrishnan TS, Sundar CS. Baseline drift removal and denoising of MCG data using EEMD: role of noise amplitude and the thresholding effect. Med Eng Phys. 2014;36(10):1266-1276.
design: Methodological parameter sensitivity and comparative denoising study
signal_type: Simulated and human 37-channel magnetocardiography (MCG) time series
decomposition: Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD) vs WT and ICA
parameters_reported: Systematic variation of EEMD added noise amplitude ratio and IMF interval thresholding
key_finding: Quantified sensitivity of EEMD mode-mixing suppression to added noise amplitude and showed interval thresholding between adjacent zero-crossings outperforms wavelet and ICA denoising at low SNR.

citation: Navarro X, Porée F, Beuchée A, Carrault G. Denoising preterm EEG by signal decomposition and adaptive filtering: a comparative study. Med Eng Phys. 2015;37(3):315-320.
design: Comparative methodological study on synthetic and clinical neonatal signals
signal_type: Synthetic neonatal EEG and clinical preterm infant EEG
decomposition: EMD, CEEMDAN, and DWT combined with adaptive filtering
parameters_reported: Not reported
key_finding: CEEMDAN mitigates mode mixing inherent to plain EMD in non-stationary preterm EEG, reducing RMSE by up to 30% when paired with adaptive filtering.

citation: Huang NE, Hu K, Yang ACC, Chang HC, Jia D, Liang WK, Yeh JR, Kao CL, Juan CH, Peng CK, Meijer JH, Wang YH, Long SR, Wu Z. On Holo-Hilbert spectral analysis: a full informational spectral representation for nonlinear and non-stationary data. Philos Trans A Math Phys Eng Sci. 2016;374(2065):20150206.
design: Foundational theoretical and methodological paper introducing Holo-Hilbert Spectral Analysis
signal_type: Synthetic additive and multiplicative AM-FM signals, Duffing oscillator, turbulence, and physiological recordings
decomposition: Two-layer nested EMD/EEMD + NHT/DQ -> Holo-Hilbert Spectrum H(t, f_c, f_AM)
parameters_reported: Layer-1 EMD/EEMD carrier IMFs; cubic spline envelope extraction; Layer-2 EMD/EEMD AM modes; NHT/DQ phase differentiation; physical admissibility f_AM < f_c enforced
key_finding: Established the HHSA framework by applying a second-layer EMD to amplitude envelopes of first-layer IMFs, creating a 3-D spectrum H(t, f_c, f_AM) that simultaneously resolves additive oscillations, intra-wave FM, and multiplicative cross-scale AM.

citation: Hou TY, Shi Z. Extracting a shape function for a signal with intra-wave frequency modulation. Philos Trans A Math Phys Eng Sci. 2016;374(2065):20150194.
design: Mathematical and algorithmic study with synthetic and physiological benchmarks
signal_type: Synthetic intra-wave FM signals, Stokes wave, noisy Duffing equation, and 16-s human ECG recording
decomposition: Sparse time-frequency shape-function extraction via SVD in phase space compared against EMD and EEMD
parameters_reported: Local phase window width mu = 3 periods; envelope smoothness lambda = 1/2; rank-1 SVD in phase coordinates
key_finding: Proved that ensemble averaging in EEMD smooths out sharp intra-wave FM, whereas extracting a 2pi-periodic shape function via SVD in phase space preserves physical waveform nonlinearity and separates intra-wave from inter-wave FM.

citation: Zeng K, Chen D, Ouyang G, Wang L, Liu X, Li X. An EEMD-ICA approach to enhancing artifact rejection for noisy multivariate neural data. IEEE Trans Neural Syst Rehabil Eng. 2016;24(6):630-638.
design: Methodological algorithm evaluation on semi-simulated and clinical EEG
signal_type: Semi-simulated noisy multivariate neural signals and clinical epileptic absence-seizure EEG
decomposition: EEMD-ICA vs Wavelet-ICA (AWICA) and standard ICA
parameters_reported: Not reported
key_finding: Applying EEMD prior to ICA prevents mode mixing between artifacts and neural oscillations at low SNR, doubling SSIM and reducing RMSE.

citation: Zhang Y, Xu P, Li P, Duan K, Wen Y, Yang Q, Zhang T, Yao D. Noise-assisted multivariate empirical mode decomposition for multichannel EMG signals. Biomed Eng Online. 2017;16(1):107.
design: Comparative multichannel methodological study
signal_type: 4-channel surface electromyography (EMG) from 11 healthy subjects
decomposition: Noise-Assisted Multivariate EMD (NA-MEMD) vs MEMD and single-channel EEMD
parameters_reported: Auxiliary white-noise channels appended to 4-channel EMG projection sifting
key_finding: Single-channel EEMD yields unequal IMF counts across channels, whereas NA-MEMD guarantees identical IMF counts, cross-channel frequency alignment, and minimal mode mixing.

citation: Xu Y, Luo M, Li T, Song G. ECG signal de-noising and baseline wander correction based on CEEMDAN and wavelet threshold. Sensors (Basel). 2017;17(12):2754.
design: Methodological validation study on benchmark physiological database
signal_type: Human ECG recordings from MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database
decomposition: CEEMDAN + Wavelet Thresholding
parameters_reported: Stage-wise adaptive white noise; IMF mode classification based on autocorrelation and zero-crossing rate
key_finding: CEEMDAN resolves mode mixing in ECG decomposition, enabling simultaneous high-frequency wavelet thresholding and baseline wander removal without distorting QRS morphology.

citation: Wang YH, Hu K, Lo MT. Uniform phase empirical mode decomposition: an optimal hybridization of masking signal and ensemble approaches. IEEE Access. 2018;6:34819-34833.
design: Theoretical and algorithmic hybridization study
signal_type: Synthetic intermittent two-tone signals and real-world non-stationary recordings
decomposition: Uniform Phase Empirical Mode Decomposition (UPEMD) vs EEMD, CEEMDAN, and Masking EMD
parameters_reported: Ensemble of n_p sinusoidal masking signals with phases uniformly distributed over [0, 2pi]; deterministic disturbance amplitude epsilon_m
key_finding: Hybridizing deterministic sinusoidal masking with a multi-phase uniform ensemble over [0, 2pi] eliminates mode mixing and mode splitting with zero stochastic residual noise.

citation: Nguyen KT, Liang WK, Lee V, Chang WS, Muggleton NG, Yeh JR, Huang NE, Juan CH. Unraveling nonlinear electrophysiologic processes in the human visual system with full dimension spectral analysis. Sci Rep. 2019;9(1):16919.
design: Synthetic ground-truth validation and within-subject human SSVEP EEG study (n=13 monocular/binocular, n=14 dichoptic)
signal_type: Synthetic ground-truth AM-FM signal and human SSVEP EEG (36 channels, 1000 Hz)
decomposition: Two-layer Masking EMD + NHT/DQ (HHSA)
parameters_reported: Dyadic masking EMD for Layer 1 and 2; natural cubic spline envelope interpolation; admissibility f_AM < f_c enforced; 8 log2 bins per octave
key_finding: HHSA resolved fundamental 2 Hz AM, a nonlinear 4 Hz envelope frequency-doubling absent in stimulus inputs, and propagation of 2 Hz AM across 8-32 Hz carriers without harmonic sideband artifacts.

citation: Liu G, Hu X, Wang E, Zhou G, Cai J, Zhang S. SVR-EEMD: an improved EEMD method based on support vector regression extension in PPG signal denoising. Comput Math Methods Med. 2019;2019:5363712.
design: Methodological boundary/end-effect mitigation study
signal_type: Simulated nonlinear signals and clinical photoplethysmography (PPG) signals
decomposition: Support Vector Regression Extended Ensemble EMD (SVR-EEMD) vs standard EEMD
parameters_reported: Support Vector Regression boundary extrema extrapolation prior to EEMD sifting; correlation IMF threshold
key_finding: Spline divergence at finite signal boundaries propagates inward; extending endpoints via SVR prior to EEMD attenuates boundary distortion and improves PPG denoising SNR.

citation: Kosciessa JQ, Kloosterman NA, Garrett DD. Standard multiscale entropy reflects neural dynamics at mismatched temporal scales: what's signal irregularity got to do with it? PLoS Comput Biol. 2020;16(5):e1007885.
design: Methodological critique, simulation, and human lifespan EEG re-analysis
signal_type: Simulated 1/f noise plus narrowband oscillations and human resting EEG across lifespan
decomposition: Multiscale Entropy (MSE) coarse-graining vs spectral slope (1/f) and narrowband decomposition
parameters_reported: Embedding dimension m = 2; global vs scale-specific similarity bound r; boxcar vs Butterworth filters
key_finding: Proved that standard MSE conflates broadband 1/f spectral slope with narrowband oscillatory power at mismatched temporal scales due to boxcar coarse-graining filter roll-off.

citation: Quinn AJ, Lopes-dos-Santos V, Dupret D, Nobre AC, Woolrich MW. EMD: Empirical Mode Decomposition and Hilbert-Huang Spectral Analyses in Python. J Open Source Softw. 2021;6(59):2977.
design: Open-source software and methodological reference study
signal_type: Simulated nested AM-FM oscillations and neurophysiological LFP/MEG/EEG time series
decomposition: Plain EMD, EEMD, Masked EMD, Second-layer EMD, HHT, and Holospectrum in Python
parameters_reported: Configurable via SiftConfig dictionary (mask frequencies, amplitudes, ensemble sizes, stopping rules)
key_finding: Validated open-source Python toolbox implementing masked sifting, second-layer envelope sifting, IF/IA extraction, and sparse multidimensional Holospectrum computation.

citation: Juan CH, Nguyen KT, Liang WK, Quinn AJ, Chen YH, Muggleton NG, Yeh JR, Woolrich MW, Nobre AC, Huang NE. Revealing the dynamic nature of amplitude modulated neural entrainment with Holo-Hilbert spectral analysis. Front Neurosci. 2021;15:673369.
design: Synthetic ground-truth validation and human SSVEP EEG experiments (n=10 static, n=8 time-varying PAC)
signal_type: Simulated non-sinusoidal/PAC waveforms (1000 Hz) and human SSVEP EEG (36 channels)
decomposition: Two-layer Masking EMD + NHT/DQ (HHSA) vs Morlet wavelet and PAC Modulation Index
parameters_reported: Two-layer Masking EMD; PCHIP/cubic spline envelope normalisation; log2 frequency binning; f_AM < f_c enforced
key_finding: HHSA accurately tracks time-varying AM modulation depth (r > 0.99 with beta^2) and resolves genuine cross-frequency coupling without harmonic artifacts generated by wavelet/PAC on non-sinusoidal waveforms.

citation: Fabus MS, Quinn AJ, Warnaby CE, Woolrich MW. Automatic decomposition of electrophysiological data into distinct nonsinusoidal oscillatory modes. J Neurophysiol. 2021;126(5):1670-1684.
design: Methodological algorithm development with simulation and multispecies electrophysiological validation
signal_type: Simulated non-sinusoidal signals, rat hippocampal theta LFP, and human alpha MEG/EEG
decomposition: Iterated Masking Empirical Mode Decomposition (itEMD) vs plain EMD, EEMD, and dyadic masking EMD
parameters_reported: Data-driven iterative mask frequencies updated until convergence (<1% relative frequency change); mask amplitude matched to local SD
key_finding: Iterated masking EMD automatically adapts mask frequencies to intrinsic spectral peaks without prior tuning, overcoming mode mixing and reconstructing non-sinusoidal shape accurately.

citation: Erdiş A, Akif Bakir M, I Jaiteh M. A method for detecting the mode mixing problem in empirical mode decomposition. J Appl Stat. 2021;48(13-15):2847-2863.
design: Statistical methodology and simulation study
signal_type: Simulated mode-mixed time series and real acoustic signals
decomposition: EMD + Kaiser-filtered modified short-time Itakura-Saito spectral distance
parameters_reported: Standard EMD sifting paired with Kaiser window filtering and sub-segment Itakura-Saito distance thresholding
key_finding: Developed a quantitative diagnostic metric based on Kaiser-filtered short-time Itakura-Saito distance across IMF sub-segments to objectively detect mode mixing.

citation: Moradi N, LeVan P, Akin B, Goodyear BG, Sotero RC. Holo-Hilbert spectral-based noise removal method for EEG high-frequency bands. J Neurosci Methods. 2022;368:109470.
design: Methodological simulation study (gamma with 1/f noise) and simultaneous human EEG-fMRI validation (n=1, 256 channels)
signal_type: Simulated gamma-band EEG and human simultaneous EEG-fMRI recordings
decomposition: Two-layer ICEEMDAN applied separately to upper amplitude envelope (IMFs_AM) and FM carrier (IMFs_FM)
parameters_reported: 300 ensemble realizations; 0.2 SD noise amplitude; low-power IMF zeroing prior to inverse summation
key_finding: Extended HHSA to bidirectional filtering and reconstruction by thresholding low-power AM and FM modes, achieving high mutual information with ground truth and suppressing MR gradient artifacts.

citation: Lee PL, Lee TM, Lee WK, Chu NN, Shelepin YE, Hsu HT, Chang HH. The Full Informational Spectral Analysis for Auditory Steady-State Responses in Human Brain Using the Combination of Canonical Correlation Analysis and Holo-Hilbert Spectral Analysis. J Clin Med. 2022;11(13):3868.
design: Methodological spatial-spectral study in healthy adults (n=25; monaural 37 Hz stimulation)
signal_type: Human auditory steady-state response (ASSR) multichannel EEG (37 Hz fundamental, 74 Hz harmonic)
decomposition: Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) spatial filtering + Two-layer HHSA vs Welch Fourier PSD
parameters_reported: CCA template extraction at ASSR frequencies followed by two-layer EMD/HHSA
key_finding: CCA-HHSA cleanly isolates the 37 Hz fundamental and 74 Hz harmonic carriers along the f_c axis and resolves multiple slow AM modulating frequencies along the f_AM axis without Fourier sideband splitting.

citation: Chang WS, Liang WK, Huang NE, Nguyen KT, Juan CH. Resolving non-linear, non-stationary and non-sinusoidal oscillatory dynamics in electrophysiology using Holo-Hilbert Spectral Analysis. Biol Psychol. 2025;200:109099.
design: Methodological review of adaptive time-frequency analysis in cognitive neurophysiology
signal_type: Electrophysiological M/EEG and LFP neurophysiological time series
decomposition: Two-layer EMD/HHSA applied to amplitude envelopes (AM) and instantaneous frequency (FM shape)
parameters_reported: Not reported
key_finding: Synthesized the three core capabilities of HHSA: (1) data-driven IMF extraction, (2) cycle-by-cycle instantaneous frequency of non-sinusoidal waveforms, and (3) second-layer AM sifting separating genuine cross-frequency coupling from harmonic artifacts.

citation: Kao SC, Liang WK, Wang CH, Moreau D. Beyond the Fourier transform: capturing nonlinear neural dynamics in exercise and cognition research. Biol Psychol. 2025;201:109126.
design: Methodological perspective and comparative review
signal_type: Human electroencephalography (EEG) in exercise and cognitive neuroscience
decomposition: HHSA, CFC, and MSE vs Fourier Transform
parameters_reported: Not reported
key_finding: Compared Fourier spectral analysis against nonlinear methods (MSE, CFC, HHSA), highlighting HHSA's ability to represent non-stationary frequency shifts and cross-scale amplitude modulations without stationarity assumptions.

citation: Chu KT, Lei WC, Wu MH, Fuh JL, Wang SJ, French IT, Chang WS, Chang CF, Huang NE, Liang WK, Juan CH. A holo-spectral EEG analysis provides an early detection of cognitive decline and predicts the progression to Alzheimer's disease. Front Aging Neurosci. 2023;15:1195424.
design: Cross-sectional (n=205: 51 CN, 42 MCI, 112 AD) and 3-year longitudinal follow-up of MCI (n=72: 36 stable, 36 converted)
signal_type: Resting-state EEG (19 channels, eyes-closed/open, 6 min, 200 Hz)
decomposition: Two-layer improved CEEMDAN + DQ transform + natural cubic spline upper envelope; FOOOF comparator
parameters_reported: Dyadic filter bank 0.5-100 Hz; stopping rule <=1 extrema/zero-crossing difference
key_finding: MCI/AD showed augmented AM power in low frequencies (delta, theta) and attenuated AM power in high frequencies (beta, gamma); baseline attenuated posterior alpha/beta AM power distinguished MCI converters from non-converters (SVM sensitivity 0.90, Decision Tree specificity 0.80).

citation: Chang KH, French IT, Liang WK, Lo YS, Wang YR, Cheng ML, Huang NE, Wu HC, Lim SN, Chen CM, Juan CH. Evaluating the Different Stages of Parkinson's Disease Using Electroencephalography With Holo-Hilbert Spectral Analysis. Front Aging Neurosci. 2022;14:832637.
design: Cross-sectional case-control study (99 PD patients: 80 early, 19 late; 59 controls)
signal_type: Resting EEG (26 channels, eyes closed vs open contrast, 10 min, 2500 Hz)
decomposition: Two-layer improved CEEMDAN + DQ transform + cubic spline envelope
parameters_reported: 12 first-layer IMFs, 12 second-layer IMFs; zero mean envelope criteria
key_finding: PD patients exhibited increased theta/delta2 HHSA power and reduced beta/gamma AM power; central/parietal beta and theta AM correlated with HAM-D depression scores (r > 0.7), and Bagging classifier achieved AUC = 0.90.

citation: Liang WK, Tseng P, Yeh JR, Huang NE, Juan CH. Frontoparietal beta amplitude modulation and its interareal cross-frequency coupling in visual working memory. Neuroscience. 2021;460:69-87.
design: Within-subject crossover sham-controlled anodal tDCS visual working memory study (n=20)
signal_type: Task EEG (64 channels, 1000 Hz, ICA source clusters in mid-frontal, right-parietal, left-occipital)
decomposition: Two-layer masking EMD (eEMD) + DQ + Holo-Hilbert cross-frequency phase clustering (HHCFPC)
parameters_reported: 8 first-layer IMFs, 5 second-layer IMFs; sinusoidal masking amplitude factor in OSF hhsa_tools_d2
key_finding: Mid-frontal beta (13.5-24 Hz) AM power at theta modulating frequencies (1.8-4 Hz) correlated with VWM capacity (r = 0.66); anodal rPPC tDCS enhanced capacity in low performers by strengthening r-parietal theta phase to mid-frontal beta AM coupling.

citation: Hsu CY, Liu TL, Lee DH, Yeh DR, Chen YH, Liang WK, Juan CH. Amplitude modulating frequency overrides carrier frequency in tACS-induced phosphene percept. Hum Brain Mapp. 2023;44(3):914-926.
design: Factorial neuromodulation experiment (n=12; 2 montages x 4 carrier freqs [10-22 Hz] x 3 AM freqs [0, 2, 4 Hz])
signal_type: AM-tACS stimulation waveforms and near-eye supra-eyebrow EDA potential recordings
decomposition: Two-layer HHSA applied to near-eye EDA potentials
parameters_reported: Not reported
key_finding: AM envelope frequencies (2 and 4 Hz) overrode 10-22 Hz carrier frequencies to govern subjective perceived phosphene flash rates; HHSA of near-eye EDA confirmed shunted current from occipital tACS exceeded retinal thresholds.

citation: Chang WS, Liang WK, Li DH, Muggleton NG, Balachandran P, Huang NE, Juan CH. The association between working memory precision and the nonlinear dynamics of frontal and parieto-occipital EEG activity. Sci Rep. 2023;13(1):14252.
design: Parametric working memory load experiment (n=33; set sizes 1, 2, 4, 6 with retro-cue)
signal_type: Task EEG transformed via surface Laplacian (64 channels, 2000 Hz)
decomposition: Two-layer sinusoidal masking EMD + DQ + cross-frequency directed phase-lag index (dPLI)
parameters_reported: 4 initial masking phases (0, pi/2, pi, 3pi/2); masking amplitude = 2.0x mean pre-decomposed IMF amplitude; 10 layer-1 IMFs
key_finding: WM load suppressed parieto-occipital alpha/beta power; individual recall precision correlated positively with frontal theta power and negatively with parieto-occipital alpha/beta AM (4-12 Hz AMF), dissociating selection from representation fidelity.

citation: Tsai YC, Li CT, Juan CH. A review of critical brain oscillations in depression and the efficacy of transcranial magnetic stimulation treatment. Front Psychiatry. 2023;14:1073984.
design: Narrative review of EEG/MEG oscillations, asymmetry, PAC, and HHSA biomarkers in MDD and rTMS response
signal_type: Resting-state and task EEG/MEG in depression
decomposition: Reviews Fourier band power, FAA, theta-gamma PAC, and two-layer HHSA
parameters_reported: Not reported
key_finding: Synthesizes evidence showing inconsistent replication of single-band markers in MDD and highlights that two-layer HHSA captures prolonged iTBS-induced enhancement of prefrontal theta-alpha AM as a predictor of antidepressant response.

citation: Tsai YC, Li CT, Liang WK, Cheng CM, Jeng JS, Juan CH. Amplitude modulated gamma oscillations as electrophysiological markers for repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation efficacy in treatment-resistant depression: a randomized sham-controlled study. Int J Clin Health Psychol. 2025;25(3):100593.
design: Double-blind, randomized, sham-controlled clinical trial (n=61 TRD patients: 19 iTBS, 20 10-Hz rTMS, 22 sham)
signal_type: Resting-state eyes-closed EEG (36 channels, 1000 Hz, 5 min pre/post treatment)
decomposition: Two-layer CEEMDAN + DQ transform vs Hanning-windowed FFT (47-90 Hz)
parameters_reported: Stopping rule: zero crossings/extrema difference <=1, mean envelopes ~0
key_finding: Baseline alpha-beta AM-modulated high gamma (6.4-22.6 Hz fam | 47.3-90 Hz fc) correlated positively with depression severity (r = 0.40, p < 0.01) and was significantly lower at baseline in rTMS responders, whereas conventional FFT gamma power failed to distinguish responders.

citation: Zhang J, Villringer A, Nikulin VV. Dopaminergic Modulation of Local Non-oscillatory Activity and Global-Network Properties in Parkinson's Disease: An EEG Study. Front Aging Neurosci. 2022;14:846017.
design: Within-subject crossover ON vs OFF dopaminergic medication study in Parkinson's disease (n=15)
signal_type: Resting-state eyes-open EEG (32 channels, 512 Hz, ~3 min)
decomposition: Welch PSD + 3-step robust log-log regression for 2-45 Hz aperiodic 1/f spectral slope + lagged coherence
parameters_reported: Welch 512-sample window; 1 MAD peak exclusion for robustfit slope; proportional graph thresholds 36% to 4%
key_finding: Dopaminergic medication steepened the broadband aperiodic 1/f spectral slope in left central sensorimotor region (p = 0.022) and increased beta lagged coherence without altering oscillatory power; flatter slope predicted lower global network efficiency (rho = -0.764).

citation: Gallego-Molina NJ, Ortiz A, Martínez-Murcia FJ, Rodríguez-Rodríguez I. Unraveling Dyslexia-Related Connectivity Patterns in EEG Signals by Holo-Hilbert Spectral Analysis. In: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (Vol. 13258, pp. 43-52). Springer; 2022.
design: Case-control auditory entrainment study (n=48 children: 16 dyslexia, 32 controls)
signal_type: Task EEG during 4.8, 16, 40 Hz AM white noise (32 channels, 500 Hz, inter-channel cross-correlation signals)
decomposition: Two-layer masking EMD (Python emd package) + NHT on cross-correlation signals
parameters_reported: Not reported
key_finding: Applying two-layer masking HHSA to inter-channel EEG cross-correlation signals during 4.8 Hz AM entrainment revealed differential delta/theta PAC connectivity centered on T8 in dyslexic children, achieving AUC = 0.84 with SVM.

citation: Acharya M, Deo RC, Barua PD, Devi A, Tao X. Graph empirical mode decomposition and multiscale feature extraction for EEG-based classification of Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia. Comput Methods Programs Biomed. 2026;279:109302.
design: Cross-sectional multiclass diagnostic classification study (n=88: 36 AD, 23 FTD, 29 controls)
signal_type: Resting-state eyes-closed EEG (19 channels, 100 Hz, 0.5-40 Hz)
decomposition: Graph Empirical Mode Decomposition (GEMD) fused with GFT, GWT, and DWT
parameters_reported: Max 5 IMFs per graph frequency channel; <=1 zero-crossings/extrema difference
key_finding: Projecting multi-channel EEG onto correlation-weighted graph Laplacian eigenbasis and extracting energy and Shannon entropy from GEMD IMFs yielded 96.68% multiclass accuracy (Random Forest) and >98.6% binary accuracies via AdaBoost; ablating GEMD dropped multiclass accuracy from 93.43% to 86.71%.

citation: French IT, Chang KH, Liang WK, Chang WS, Lo YS, Wang YR, Cheng ML, Huang NE, Wu HC, Lim SN, Chen CM, Juan CH. Attentional dysfunction arises from right frontocentral and occipital network connectivity in Parkinson's disease. Neuroimage Rep. 2025;5(1):100241.
design: Case-control cognitive task EEG study in PD patients and controls performing Eriksen Flanker task
signal_type: Event-related Flanker task EEG
decomposition: Two-layer HHSA + HHT + Holo-Hilbert cross-frequency phase clustering (HHCFPC)
parameters_reported: Not reported
key_finding: During Flanker congruency, PD patients showed attenuated midfrontal theta carrier power, loss of low-frequency AM within the theta band, and reduced theta-gamma and theta-beta HHCFPC from right prefrontal cortex to contralateral frontal and occipital regions.

citation: Chou PS, Lee MY, Chang WS, Chou MC, Hsu CY, Liou LM, Juan CH, Lai CL. Potential Cognitive Decline Linked to Electronegative L5 in Type 2 Diabetes: A Holo-Hilbert Spectral Analysis. Neuroendocrinology. 2024;114(12):1124-1138.
design: Cross-sectional cohort study in type 2 diabetes mellitus (n=68: 15 normal, 39 MCI, 14 AD)
signal_type: Resting-state EEG paired with serum electronegative LDL-C subfraction (L5%) and CASI scores
decomposition: Two-layer Holo-Hilbert spectral analysis (HHSA)
parameters_reported: Not reported
key_finding: Higher electronegative LDL (L5%) was independently associated with MCI and AD risk in T2DM; in T2DM-MCI, elevated L5% correlated with poorer concentration and an HHSA shift toward increased low-frequency and reduced high-frequency oscillation power.

citation: Tsai YC, Li CT, Liang WK, Muggleton NG, Tsai CC, Huang NE, Juan CH. Critical role of rhythms in prefrontal transcranial magnetic stimulation for depression: A randomized sham-controlled study. Hum Brain Mapp. 2022;43(5):1535-1547.
design: Double-blind, randomized, sham-controlled trial in treatment-resistant depression (n=61: 19 piTBS, 20 10-Hz rTMS, 22 sham; left DLPFC)
signal_type: Resting-state EEG recorded before and after 2-week treatment
decomposition: Two-layer CEEMDAN-based Holo-Hilbert spectral analysis (HHSA)
parameters_reported: Not reported

citation: Huang YN, Liang WK, Juan CH. Spatial prediction modulates the rhythm of attentional sampling. Cereb Cortex. 2024;34(9):bhae392.
design: Within-subject cognitive visuospatial attention experiment manipulating cue validity (100% vs 50%)

citation: Ho CN, Huang NE, Chen JY, Yang AC. Exploring nociceptive-analgesic balance and EEG modulation patterns during general anesthesia using Holo-Hilbert spectral analysis. Pain Res Manag. 2026;2026:5504074.

citation: Liu J, Zhang W, Hu S, Wu C, Dong K, Wei Q, Wang G, Fang J, Zhang D, Lan M, Zhang F, Sun H. Analysis of Amplitude Modulation of EEG Based on Holo-Hilbert Spectrum Analysis During General Anesthesia. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng. 2024;71(5):1607-1616.

citation: Jaiswal S, Huang SL, Juan CH, Huang NE, Liang WK. Resting state dynamics in people with varying degrees of anxiety and mindfulness: A nonlinear and nonstationary perspective. Neuroscience. 2023;519:177-197.

citation: Hsu HT, Lee WK, Shyu KK, Yeh TK, Chang CY, Lee PL. Analyses of EEG Oscillatory Activities During Slow and Fast Repetitive Movements Using Holo-Hilbert Spectral Analysis. IEEE Trans Neural Syst Rehabil Eng. 2018;26(9):1659-1668.

citation: Fraga FJ, Falk TH, Kanda PAM, Anghinah R. Characterizing Alzheimer's disease severity via resting-awake EEG amplitude modulation analysis. PLoS One. 2013;8(8):e72240.

parameters_reported: Not reported

citation: Jesus B Jr, Cassani R, McGeown WJ, Cecchi M, Fadem KC, Falk TH. Multimodal Prediction of Alzheimer's Disease Severity Level Based on Resting-State EEG and Structural MRI. Front Hum Neurosci. 2021;15:700627.

parameters_reported: Not reported

citation: López-Azcárate J, Tainta M, Rodríguez-Oroz MC, Valencia M, González R, Guridi J, Iriarte J, Obeso JA, Artieda J, Alegre M. Coupling between beta and high-frequency activity in the human subthalamic nucleus may be a pathophysiological mechanism in Parkinson's disease. J Neurosci. 2010;30(19):6667-6677.

parameters_reported: Not reported
key_finding: In the parkinsonian OFF state, STN high-frequency oscillations (~300 Hz) were pathologically phase-locked to abnormal beta phase, suppressing movement-related HFO AM in proportion to bradykinesia/rigidity; dopaminergic therapy (ON state) abolished beta-HFO PAC and restored movement-related gamma/HFO amplitude modulation.

citation: Bernardi D, Casula EP, Rocchi L, Fadiga L, Koch G, Papo D. Multivariate empirical mode decomposition reveals markers of Alzheimer's disease in the oscillatory response to transcranial magnetic stimulation. Clin Neurophysiol. 2025;176:2110756.

decomposition: Single-layer Multivariate Empirical Mode Decomposition (MEMD) + Hilbert transform
parameters_reported: Not reported
key_finding: MEMD of DLPFC TMS-EEG revealed weakened slow-frequency responses and blunted biphasic fast oscillatory modes in AD patients compared to controls, enabling an SVM classifier to achieve an 85% true positive rate (23% false positive rate).

citation: Wan W, Gu Z, Peng CK, Cui X. Beyond Frequency Bands: Complementary-Ensemble-Empirical-Mode-Decomposition-Enhanced Microstate Sequence Non-Randomness Analysis for Aiding Diagnosis and Cognitive Prediction of Dementia. Brain Sci. 2024;14(5):487.
design: Cross-sectional case-control diagnostic and cognitive prediction study (AD, FTD, and healthy controls)
signal_type: Resting-state multi-channel EEG
decomposition: Single-layer Complementary Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (CEEMD) integrated with EEG microstate sequence non-randomness index (MSNRI)
parameters_reported: Not reported
key_finding: Dementia patients exhibited more random spatiotemporal microstate transitions than controls (MSNRI: HC 6.958 vs FTD 5.756, p < 0.01; HC vs AD 5.462, p < 0.001); integrating scale-specific CEEMD decomposition with microstate non-randomness features predicted MMSE cognitive scores with R^2 = 0.940.

citation: Tsai PH, Lin C, Tsao J, Lin PF, Wang PC, Huang NE, Lo MT. Empirical mode decomposition based detrended sample entropy in electroencephalography for Alzheimer's disease. J Neurosci Methods. 2012;210(2):230-237.
design: Observational clinical cohort study in Alzheimer's disease (n=27 baseline; n=5 with 6-month longitudinal follow-up)
signal_type: Resting-awake EEG (30 min recording, 30 s epochs)
decomposition: Single-layer Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) detrending combined with Sample Entropy (detrended-SaEn)
parameters_reported: Not reported
key_finding: Removing non-stationary trends via EMD prior to Sample Entropy calculation revealed significant positive correlations with MMSE scores across frontal/temporal electrodes (Fp1, Fp2, F4, T3; r = 0.361-0.523, p < 0.05) and tracked 6-month longitudinal MMSE changes at F7 (r = 0.975, p < 0.05).

citation: Echeverría JC, Crowe JA, Woolfson MS, Hayes-Gill BR. Application of empirical mode decomposition to heart rate variability analysis. Med Biol Eng Comput. 2001;39(4):471-479.
design: Methodological simulation (IPFM and chirp signals) and experimental human validation under controlled metronomic breathing (n=14)
signal_type: Short-term ECG-derived RR interval time series and simulated IPFM beat series
decomposition: Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) + Hilbert Transform (HHT spectrum of instantaneous amplitude and frequency)
parameters_reported: Standard sifting stopping criterion; 4 dominant IMFs; instantaneous frequency error < 0.22% on synthetic signals
sampling_resampling: Even resampling / interpolation of unequal beat-to-beat RR intervals and IPFM occurrence times prior to EMD sifting
key_finding: EMD combined with Hilbert transform isolates non-stationary and nonlinear amplitude- and frequency-modulated HRV components into physiologically meaningful IMFs with <0.22% frequency tracking error, overcoming stationarity and linearity assumptions of Fourier PSD.
device: Laboratory ECG system
reference_standard: Simulated ground-truth IPFM/chirp modulation and paced breathing frequency protocol
agreement_metric: Instantaneous frequency error < 0.22% relative to synthetic ground truth; direct tracking of paced breathing rate transitions

citation: Souza Neto EP, Custaud MA, Cejka JC, Abry P, Frutoso J, Gharib C, Flandrin P. Assessment of cardiovascular autonomic control by the empirical mode decomposition. Methods Inf Med. 2004;43(1):60-65.
design: Experimental physiological validation study during postural tilt testing in healthy humans
signal_type: Beat-to-beat RR interval time series across supine-to-standing postural transitions
decomposition: Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) time-varying data-adaptive filtering
parameters_reported: Local extrema spline envelope sifting; adaptive mode selection separating respiratory and sympathetic-baroreflex scales
sampling_resampling: Beat-to-beat tachogram processed directly via local extrema interpolation during EMD sifting
key_finding: EMD provides a local, fully data-driven separation of HF and LF cardiovascular oscillations without requiring fixed cutoffs, accurately tracking rapid autonomic shifts during postural transitions where stationary Fourier methods blur transients.
device: Laboratory ECG monitor
reference_standard: Standard Fourier/wavelet time-frequency spectral analysis during orthostatic tilt challenge
agreement_metric: Qualitative and quantitative concordance of time-varying LF and HF power trajectories across tilt transitions

citation: de Souza Neto EP, Abry P, Loiseau P, Cejka JC, Custaud MA, Frutoso J, Gharib C, Flandrin P. Empirical mode decomposition to assess cardiovascular autonomic control in rats. Fundam Clin Pharmacol. 2007;21(5):481-496.
design: Pharmacological autonomic blockade validation study in conscious normotensive Wistar rats (phentolamine, atropine, atenolol)
signal_type: Beat-to-beat RR interval and systolic blood pressure variability time series
decomposition: Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) + Hilbert instantaneous amplitude/frequency estimation
parameters_reported: IMF-based LF and HF spectral energy ratios across baseline and selective pharmacological blockade epochs
sampling_resampling: Continuous arterial pressure and ECG beat-to-beat interval extraction with spline-based EMD sifting
band_definitions: Data-adaptive IMF bands corresponding to rodent LF and HF autonomic bands without rigid cutoffs
key_finding: Pharmacological blockade confirmed that EMD-derived LF and HF indices accurately quantify selective sympathetic and parasympathetic modulation under non-stationary physiological conditions.
device: Implantable telemetry / arterial catheterization and ECG
reference_standard: Selective pharmacological autonomic blockade (atropine, atenolol, phentolamine) and FFT
agreement_metric: Statistically significant directional changes in EMD LF and HF indices matching selective receptor blockade (p < 0.05)

citation: Magagnin V, Bassani T, Lucini D, Pagani M, Caiani EG, Cerutti S, Porta A. Empirical mode decomposition to assess baroreflex gain from spontaneous variability during exercise in humans. Annu Int Conf IEEE Eng Med Biol Soc. 2009;2009:2236-2239.
design: Experimental human physiology study during incremental dynamic bicycle exercise
signal_type: Spontaneous heart period (HP / RR) and systolic arterial pressure (SAP) beat-to-beat variability series
decomposition: Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) for oscillatory mode isolation + baroreflex alpha-index transfer gain estimation
parameters_reported: Mode-specific HP and SAP variance and cross-spectral coherence in LF and HF IMFs across exercise loads
sampling_resampling: Beat-to-beat HP (ms) and SAP (mmHg) series decomposed on a beat-by-beat basis
band_definitions: LF: 0.04-0.15 Hz; HF: 0.15-0.40 Hz (isolated via IMF characteristic scales)
key_finding: EMD-based baroreflex sensitivity estimation effectively handles exercise-induced non-stationarities and baseline drifts, tracking progressive vagal withdrawal and baroreflex gain reduction during incremental exercise.
device: Laboratory ECG and Finapres continuous noninvasive arterial pressure monitor
reference_standard: Traditional autoregressive (AR) spectral and baroreflex sequence methods
agreement_metric: Consistent progressive reduction in baroreflex gain across incremental workload stages with superior robustness to non-stationary drift

citation: Li H, Kwong S, Yang L, Huang D, Xiao D. Hilbert-Huang transform for analysis of heart rate variability in cardiac health. IEEE/ACM Trans Comput Biol Bioinform. 2011;8(6):1557-1567.
design: Methodological simulation + human pharmacological autonomic blockade study (n=7: atropine and metoprolol)
signal_type: Short-term ECG RR interval tachograms (5 min) and synthetic multi-component modulated signals
decomposition: Cubic spline resampling + EMD + Hilbert-Huang Transform (HHT) and Hilbert Marginal Spectrum (HMS)
parameters_reported: HMS band powers (LF, HF, TP), normalized units (LF/TP, HF/TP), and LF/HF ratio before and after blockade
sampling_resampling: Explicitly proves via simulation that interpolation and uniform resampling (4 Hz) of unevenly spaced RR intervals is essential prior to HHT to prevent instantaneous frequency distortion
key_finding: Demonstrated that uniform resampling of uneven RR series is required before HHT and that HHT/HMS indices discriminate pharmacological parasympathetic and sympathetic blockade with higher sensitivity than traditional FFT power spectral density.
device: Clinical multi-lead ECG system
reference_standard: Selective intravenous pharmacological autonomic blockade (atropine and metoprolol) and Welch/FFT PSD
agreement_metric: Significant separation of pre- vs post-blockade HF/TP and LF/HF ratios (p < 0.05), outperforming stationary PSD

citation: Ebrahimi F, Setarehdan SK, Ayala-Moyeda J, Nazeran H. Automatic sleep staging using empirical mode decomposition, discrete wavelet transform, time-domain, and nonlinear dynamics features of heart rate variability signals. Comput Methods Programs Biomed. 2013;112(1):47-57.
design: Observational polysomnography cohort study (n=30 overnight recordings from Sleep Heart Health Study)
signal_type: Nocturnal ECG-derived HRV segmented into standard 5-min and ultra-short 0.5-min (30 s) epochs across sleep stages
decomposition: Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) normalized IMF band energy extraction, DWT, and nonlinear complexity features
parameters_reported: Normalized energy and instantaneous amplitude/frequency features of IMFs 1-4; ANOVA class separability criteria
sampling_resampling: Uniformly resampled RR tachograms analyzed in 300 s (5 min) vs 30 s (0.5 min) windows
band_definitions: VLF: < 0.04 Hz; LF: 0.04-0.15 Hz; HF: 0.15-0.40 Hz mapped onto EMD IMFs and DWT sub-bands
key_finding: Time-frequency features derived from EMD and DWT achieved higher sleep-stage discrimination than classical linear HRV metrics in 5-min epochs, while shortening windows from 5 min to 30 s degraded nonlinear and lower-frequency IMF separability.
device: Overnight polysomnography ECG
reference_standard: Expert R&K polysomnographic sleep stage annotations (SHHS database)
agreement_metric: Multi-class sleep staging classification accuracy and ANOVA F-statistic separability across 5-min vs 0.5-min epochs

citation: Bari V, Cairo B, De Maria B, Tonon D, Rossato G, Faes L, Porta A. An Empirical Mode Decomposition Approach to Assess the Strength of Heart Period-Systolic Arterial Pressure Variability Interactions. Annu Int Conf IEEE Eng Med Biol Soc. 2020;2020:2573-2576.
design: Experimental physiological study in healthy humans at supine rest and during 60-degree head-up tilt (n=13)
signal_type: Spontaneous beat-to-beat heart period (HP / RR) and systolic arterial pressure (SAP) variability series
decomposition: Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) separating fast respiratory mode (IMF1) and slower residual oscillations (RES) + cross-correlation
parameters_reported: Maximum cross-correlation coefficient r_max and lag between HP and SAP in original series, IMF1, and RES
sampling_resampling: Beat-to-beat HP and SAP series (250-300 consecutive beats per condition)
band_definitions: HF: 0.15-0.40 Hz (IMF1); LF & VLF: < 0.15 Hz (RES)
key_finding: EMD separated fast respiratory cardiorespiratory coupling (dominant in IMF1 at rest) from slower baroreflex-mediated HP-SAP interactions (dominant in RES and amplified during tilt).
device: Laboratory ECG and Finapres continuous blood pressure monitor
reference_standard: Unfiltered time-domain cross-correlation across supine and head-up tilt states
agreement_metric: Significant increase in slow-mode (RES) HP-SAP coupling during tilt (p < 0.05) vs predominance of IMF1 coupling at rest

citation: Lee S, Hwang HB, Park S, Kim S, Ha JH, Jang Y, Hwang S, Park HK, Lee J, Kim IY. Mental Stress Assessment Using Ultra Short Term HRV Analysis Based on Non-Linear Method. Biosensors (Basel). 2022;12(7):465.
design: Experimental human stress reactivity and ultra-short-term HRV validation study using TSST (n=74)
signal_type: ECG-derived RR interval series analyzed across 5 min, 3 min, 2 min, and 1 min windows
decomposition: Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) into first 4 IMFs + nonlinear entropy (SampEn, PermEn) + SVM
parameters_reported: Energy of IMF1-IMF4, SampEn, PermEn, RMSSD, SDNN, pNN50, LF, HF, LF/HF across windows
sampling_resampling: R-peak detection from ECG followed by cubic spline interpolation for feature extraction across 60, 120, 180, and 300 s segments
band_definitions: VLF: 0.003-0.04 Hz; LF: 0.04-0.15 Hz; HF: 0.15-0.40 Hz; plus IMF1-IMF4 energy bands
key_finding: Combining EMD IMF energy features with nonlinear and time-domain metrics in ultra-short-term (<5 min) recordings achieved 90.54% stress detection accuracy (exceeding 86.49% accuracy of standard 5-min linear HRV), validating EMD on ultra-short HRV windows.
device: Wearable/ambulatory ECG sensor
reference_standard: Standard 5-min HRV analysis and validated Trier Social Stress Test (TSST) protocol
agreement_metric: Ultra-short-term (2-3 min) SVM classification accuracy of 90.54% vs 86.49% at 5 min

citation: Saleem S, Khandoker AH, Alkhodari M, Hadjileontiadis LJ, Jelinek HF. A two-step pre-processing tool to remove Gaussian and ectopic noise for heart rate variability analysis. Sci Rep. 2022;12(1):18396.
design: Methodological signal processing and artifact sensitivity benchmark using MIT-BIH NSR database with noise/ectopic injection
signal_type: ECG and beat-to-beat RR interval series corrupted by white Gaussian noise (SNR 6-30 dB) and ectopic beats (1%-6%)
decomposition: Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN) + rank-order mean and adaptive filtering
parameters_reported: 24 HRV metrics across time-domain, frequency-domain, Poincaré, and fragmentation indices
sampling_resampling: CEEMDAN applied to ECG/RR series with two-step ectopic beat replacement prior to 4 Hz spline resampling for PSD
key_finding: CEEMDAN preprocessing restored noisy and ectopic-corrupted HRV signals with r = 0.846 and RMSE = 7.69e-5 at 6% ectopic contamination, whereas uncleaned ectopic beats severely biased Total Power, LF power, and HF power.
device: Holter ECG (MIT-BIH Normal Sinus Rhythm Database)
reference_standard: Noise-free annotated reference RR intervals from MIT-BIH database
agreement_metric: Pearson r = 0.846, RMSE = 7.69e-5 between CEEMDAN-reconstructed and ground-truth clean HRV under 6 dB Gaussian + 6% ectopic noise

citation: Grinevich AA, Chemeris NK. Spectral Analysis of Heart Rate Variability Based on the Hilbert-Huang Method. Dokl Biochem Biophys. 2023;511(1):169-172.
design: Methodological and physiological comparative study of human HRV (Hilbert-Huang Transform vs classical Fourier spectral analysis)
signal_type: Human RR interval (cardiorhythmogram) time series
decomposition: Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) + Hilbert-Huang Transform (HHT) instantaneous frequency and marginal spectrum analysis
parameters_reported: Mean instantaneous frequencies, Gaussian frequency distributions of individual IMFs, and adaptive inter-band boundaries
sampling_resampling: Resampled cardiorhythmogram decomposed into complete IMF set via EMD
band_definitions: Four intrinsic Gaussian-like spectral clusters matching HF, LF, VLF, and ULF, but with subject-specific floating boundaries
key_finding: HHT demonstrates that human HRV naturally organizes into four Gaussian-distributed frequency clusters matching HF, LF, VLF, and ULF divisions, but with individual floating boundaries that fixed Fourier frequency windows misclassify.
device: Laboratory ECG recorder
reference_standard: Task Force (1996) fixed-band Fourier Power Spectral Density
agreement_metric: Goodness-of-fit of Gaussian instantaneous frequency distributions across the 4 HHT spectral clusters vs fixed Task Force cutoffs

citation: Delgado-Aranda R, Dorantes-Méndez G, Bianchi AM, Kortelainen JM, Coelli S, Jimenez-Cruz J, Méndez MO. Assessing cardiovascular stress based on heart rate variability in female shift workers: a multiscale-multifractal analysis approach. Front Neuroergon. 2024;5:1382919.
design: Observational sleep cohort study comparing female shift workers (n=11) and daytime non-shift workers (n=7; total n=18)
signal_type: Whole-sleep ECG RR interval series
decomposition: Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) into autonomic IMFs followed by Multiscale-Multifractal Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (MMF-DFA)
parameters_reported: Scaling exponents alpha(q, tau) across scales tau = 8 to 2048 s and orders q = -5 to +5 on IMF1, IMF2-3, and IMF4
sampling_resampling: Beat-to-beat RR series decomposed into IMFs; multifractal scaling evaluated over scales tau = 8 s to 2048 s
band_definitions: IMF1: HF band (0.15-0.40 Hz); IMF2-IMF3: LF band (0.04-0.15 Hz); IMF4: VLF band (0.003-0.04 Hz)
key_finding: Combining EMD with MMF-DFA isolated scale-specific autonomic alterations in shift workers during sleep—specifically altered short-scale (<64 s) fractal dynamics in IMF1 and IMF2-3 and long-scale (>1024 s) dynamics in IMF1—that were invisible to conventional linear HRV.
device: Ambulatory sleep ECG recorder
reference_standard: Daytime worker control group and conventional time/frequency HRV indices
agreement_metric: Statistically significant group differences in IMF-specific MMF-DFA scaling exponents at tau < 64 s and tau > 1024 s (p < 0.05)

citation: Cassirame J, Vanhaesebrouck R, Chevrolat S, Mourot L. Accuracy of the Garmin 920 XT HRM to perform HRV analysis. Australas Phys Eng Sci Med. 2017;40(4):831-839.
design: Criterion device validation study across supine rest, orthostatic standing, and moderate cycling exercise (n=11)
signal_type: Beat-to-beat RR interval series recorded simultaneously by Garmin system and criterion laboratory ECG
decomposition: Time-domain, Poincaré plot, and Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) spectral HRV analysis
parameters_reported: RR interval bias/LoA, SDNN, RMSSD, pNN50, Poincaré SD1 and SD2, LF power, HF power, and LF/HF ratio
sampling_resampling: Beat-to-beat RR tachogram exported from Garmin .FIT files, aligned beat-by-beat with 1000 Hz ECG R-peaks, and spline-interpolated for PSD
key_finding: Garmin beat-to-beat RR intervals showed near-zero bias (~0.01 ms) and narrow limits of agreement (-2.24 to +2.26 ms) at supine rest with no significant differences in any derived HRV metric, whereas standing and exercise widened LoA and introduced minor HF/SD1 deviations.

reference_standard: ADInstruments PowerLab 3-lead laboratory ECG (1000 Hz)
agreement_metric: Bland-Altman RR bias (95% LoA): supine 0.01 ms (-2.24 to +2.26 ms); standing -0.01 ms (-3.12 to +3.11 ms); exercise -0.01 ms (-4.43 to +4.40 ms); non-significant HRV differences in supine rest

citation: Hernando D, Roca S, Sancho J, Alesanco Á, Bailón R. Validation of the Apple Watch for Heart Rate Variability Measurements during Relax and Mental Stress in Healthy Subjects. Sensors (Basel). 2018;18(8):2619.
design: Experimental device validation study during controlled relaxation and Stroop mental stress tasks (n=20)
signal_type: Wrist optical PPG beat-to-beat interbeat intervals (IBI / HKHeartbeatSeries) from Apple Watch vs reference RR intervals
decomposition: Gap-aware time-domain and frequency-domain (interpolated PSD and Lomb-Scargle / gap-segmented) HRV analysis

device: Apple Watch wrist PPG (HealthKit beat-to-beat heartbeat series)
reference_standard: Validated Polar H7 chest strap RR interval recorder
agreement_metric: Reliability and concordance/agreement coefficients > 0.90 for time-domain HRV; significant LF and HF bias if >5 s missing-beat gaps are bridged without segmentation

citation: Miller DJ, Sargent C, Roach GD. A Validation of Six Wearable Devices for Estimating Sleep, Heart Rate and Heart Rate Variability in Healthy Adults. Sensors (Basel). 2022;22(16):6317.

sampling_resampling: Wearable optical PPG interbeat intervals summarized over nocturnal rest epochs vs 30-s PSG/ECG epochs

key_finding: Consumer wrist wearables including Garmin Forerunner 245 Music and Apple Watch Series 6 demonstrated high nocturnal HR validity and acceptable resting/sleep HRV (RMSSD) agreement against gold-standard ECG in healthy adults.
device: Apple Watch Series 6, Garmin Forerunner 245 Music, Polar Vantage V, Oura Ring Gen 2, WHOOP 3.0, Somfit
reference_standard: Gold-standard laboratory polysomnography (PSG) with multi-lead ECG
agreement_metric: Bland-Altman bias/LoA and ICC for nocturnal HR and HRV (RMSSD); sleep-wake kappa = 0.30 (Apple Watch S6) and 0.35 (Garmin Forerunner 245)

citation: Martín Gómez R, Allevard E, Kamstra H, Cotter J, Lamb P. Validity and Reliability of Movesense HR+ ECG Measurements for High-Intensity Running and Cycling. Sensors (Basel). 2024;24(17):5713.
